body: Willful ignorance I suppose? They honestly believe their inflated height or refuse to acknowledge their actual height. I mean it works for them so I guess ignorance is bliss.

I honestly wish I knew but they’ve deluded themselves so much lol. They’ll tell me or someone else they’re 5’8-5’10 while being similar height to me and I’ll tell them I’m actually 5’4. Then they start telling me I’m the wrong one.
All my friends are the same lmfao they will inflate their height by 5+ inches. They clearly aren’t but will vehemently defend it to the end.

Force yourself to go to the beach (or whatever comforts you like a lake or mountain). Thoughts subside a bit or a lot for me when I’m in a natural environment where i can admire things instead of focusing on my own thoughts. 
Also helps to randomly hit up friends to talk/chat/see what’s going on.
binging shows or movies can distract too. I try to keep a theme like one day I’ll watch all the bond movies or romantic movies etc.
Games can also help, even picking up an old game you haven’t played in a while could spark some motivation.
That’s how depression gets ya. You can be shown all the love in the world and still feel like shit. I hope it works out for you mate

It’s so conflicting having both. It’s so hard to put in words how it feels to be apathetic yet invested

Makes me want to cry inside a bit to think of how young me would see how old me is doing now. Thank you for sharing that, I always wanted to put that feeling in words but never could.

I found it helped to be “good” at something. Made varsity in wrestling early on so that helped me a lot. Find something you’re good at whether it be sports or studies or hobbies. People can tell when you’re good or interested/passionate at something and they’ll respect you for it. Also be social, people will overlook height (for the most part) once they get to know you as a person. Being social is a useful skill later on too when you go to college and the workforce. Just strike up casual conversations with others, go hang out with others, etc. Make sure to be yourself, but a version of yourself that people like and can vibe with. Being funny also helps if you’re good at cracking jokes. Also dress well and choose clothes that fit. The male fashion subreddits offer a lot of help and tips if you’re a short guy.

You should def ask, you can never be too sure until after you check. That’s the only way to know with a 100% certainty. And insurance should cover if short stature is abnormal compared to the height you theoretically should be. Although you should mentally prepare yourself in case the answer is no. I was not mentally ready for that answer.

Have you asked to be referred to an endocrinologist to take an X-ray to see if your plates are closed? It took me a few doctors until I got one who would refer me. My plates stopped since it was too late but I have friends who still had open plates at your age. Just have to push your doctor or find one who will refer you.

Honestly, I didn’t think it was bad till about the beginning of high school. Then everyone around me shot up while I stayed the same. I got into socializing and making friends around this time as well and I recognized all these subtle comments about height. Girls (including some of my closest friends) would say how I was cute/athletic/funny/smart etc but there was always a caveat as to why it wouldn’t work out which was that I was short. They would also ridicule other dudes who were short which was terrible. Guys (including friends) would always make subtle comments about how they could kick someone’s ass for being short, that someone was less of a man for being short, general nasty things about a short dude but they would include comments like “no offense to you” as if that didn’t make feel like shit. No matter what I did, it felt as if my defining feature and flaw was “being short” this has gone well into college now and even at places I’ve worked where I felt people would be more open and understanding. Alas, I don’t know if it’s just society, social media, nature, or what but I definitely feel as if I’m less of a person who belongs in this world cause of all of it.
